description: Cross-reference graph of named people, institutions, and places in the Mayhew extract. Edges go from a canonical character file (kind: 'character') to someone/something mentioned within that testimony (kind: 'mentioned', 'institution', 'location'). Use for relationship visualisations, dramatis personae, or NPC scaffolding.

to.label: The old un (his rescuer and mentor)

edges.description: The shore-worker who pulled the tosher out of the Cuckold's Point mud as a child, later re-found him after he ran from his blacksmith apprenticeship, equipped him with bag and hoe-pole, and taught him the shore and sewers.

Worked the Parliament Houses fire rubbish in Hyde Park with him in 1834–35 — £3+ each per day. They quarrelled over the whacking (split), the fight ended their access, and the remaining rubbish was buried.

to.label: Lanky Bill, Long Tom, One-eyed George, Short-armed Jack

edges.description: Other shore-workers named in the Mayhew framing at the start of the tosher's chapter — nicknames they are "known to every one" by.
"A chap as the rats tackled in the sewers; they bit him hawfully... him as the watermen went in arter when they heard him a shouting as they was a rowin' by."
"The man as was found in the sewers about twelve year ago — the rats eat every bit of him, and left nothink but his bones." Twelve years before 1851 places this around 1839.
Buying contact — gave him £7 10s for the metal-plated bracelets from the Hyde Park rubbish, and £1 5s for the gold chain from Bishop Bonner's Fields.
The Old Gravel-lane mud-lark gang captain J.C. ran with before his rescue. In prison at time of Mayhew's interview — caught stealing bacon.
Gang mates named by J.C. at the Wapping Ragged School interview.
The printing firm (Punch, most of Dickens) where J.C. was placed as an apprentice after his Ragged School rescue — the redemption arc's outcome.
The missing-heir pure-finder whose story the widow tells — lodged in Blue Anchor Yard, Bermondsey. Real name never disclosed.

to.label: Neptune East Indiaman, bound for Bombay

edges.description: Her first husband's ship — drowned, the origin of her downward slide into pure-finding.
Sall — deaf sifter, out-shovels her partner. Only woman named outright in the extract.
"The only one in the yard as can read" — named as the literate dustman by the narrator.
Real Victorian railway contractors — the Liverpool-Irish grubber's Paris and Rouen Railway job, from which he was cheated out of £12 savings.
Source of the scar on his hand — the corpse snagged on his drag-chain at Church Hole. Dredgers were paid a parish reward per body recovered.
The rare literate dredger named in the chapter 06 narration — an anomaly in an otherwise illiterate trade.
